mainTopic: Witnesses and ייעוד on the ox, inciting another's dog, and the משנה about קרן in רשות הניזק (רבי טרפון vs. the חכמים)
overview: This amud has three topics. First, the גמרא finishes a proof that ייעוד (the warning that turns a תם ox into a מועד) is placed on the ox and not on the owner. The proof uses a ברייתא about three sets of witnesses who all came on one day. רב כהנא challenges it, and the גמרא answers three ways: the witnesses signaled to each other, they came one right after another (רב אשי), or they knew the owner but not the ox (רבינא). Next, the גמרא asks whether a dog's owner pays when someone else sets the dog on a person. Two proofs are brought and both are rejected. רבא then rules that if the victim set the dog on himself, the owner is פטור, and he explains that ריש לקיש's case of two cows is different from his rule. Finally, a new משנה brings a מחלוקת about an ox that gores in the victim's property. רבי טרפון uses a קל וחומר to argue for נזק שלם, the חכמים answer with דיו לבא מן הדין להיות כנדון, and רבי טרפון's reply continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If forewarning were on the man, the first witnesses could say they never knew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its proof from the ברייתא. If ייעוד were placed on the owner, the testimonies would have to come on three separate days. Then the first witnesses could fairly say they had no idea others would come later.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say the warning is to forewarn the man, then the first witnesses could say: 'Did we know that three days later these other witnesses would come and make him a מועד?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof that ייעוד is on the ox. It shows that the other option, ייעוד on the man, does not fit the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ייעוד is on the man, he must be warned on three different days, so the three sets of witnesses came days apart. The early witnesses could then not be blamed for the full-damage result, because they could not know others would follow. Since the ברייתא does hold them responsible together, the witnesses must have come on one day, and that only works if ייעוד is on the ox.

keyTerms.meaning: To make 'forewarned' (מועד), to place the warning status
The man, meaning the ox's owner
Those first ones, meaning the first set of witnesses
Three days

steps.confusionAlert: This step starts in the middle of an argument. The first half (ייעוד on the ox works fine) came just before this text, and here the גמרא shows why the other side fails.

phrases.english: But if you say it is to forewarn the man,
let those first ones say:
Did we know
that after three days
these would come and make him forewarned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof from the ברייתא that began before this text
steps.raayaObject: ייעוד is placed on the ox, not on the owner
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of three sets of witnesses who are all held responsible together, which works only if they came on the same day

steps.title: רב כהנא: even if forewarning is on the ox, the last witnesses have an excuse
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that he told this proof to רב כהנא, who objected. Even if ייעוד is on the ox and everyone came on one day, the last witnesses could say they only came to make the owner pay חצי נזק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I said this teaching before רב כהנא, and he said to me: And does it work well if it is to forewarn the ox? The last witnesses could also say: 'How were we supposed to know that everyone standing in court came to testify about this ox? We came only to make the man pay half damage!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא attacks the proof. He shows the same problem also exists if ייעוד is on the ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the idea that witnesses who came on one day know about each other, but רב כהנא says being in court together does not prove that. The last set could claim they came only about one goring, worth just חצי נזק, so they should not be blamed for the full damage. Steps 3-5 answer this challenge and keep the proof standing.

keyTerms.meaning: I said this teaching
Does it work well? (a challenge that it does not)
Those last ones, meaning the last set of witnesses
Half damage (חצי נזק), what a תם owner pays
The court

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I said this teaching before Rav Kahana,
and he said to me:
And to forewarn the ox, does it work well?!
Let those last ones say:
How were we to know
that all who are standing in court
came to testify about the ox?

phrases.aramaic: אֲנַן לְחַיּוֹבֵי גַּבְרָא פַּלְגָא נִזְקָא אָתֵינַן!
phrases.english: We came to make the man pay half damage!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof made in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that witnesses who came on the same day must have known about each other
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even on one day, the last witnesses could claim they came only to obligate חצי נזק, so the ברייתא is hard even if ייעוד is on the ox

steps.title: The witnesses were signaling to each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא speaks about witnesses who were seen hinting to one another, so clearly they knew they were all there to make the ox a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where they were signaling hints to each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב כהנא's challenge by narrowing the case in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the witnesses were seen signaling to each other, they cannot claim they did not know about the others. So all the sets knew together that they were making the ox a מועד, and they can all be blamed as עדים זוממין.

keyTerms.meaning: They were signaling hints to one another

phrases.english: Where they were signaling hints.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's challenge in step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The last witnesses could claim they knew nothing about the others
steps.terutzMaskana: Since they were seen signaling to each other, they knew, and the claim does not work

steps.title: רב אשי: the witnesses came one right after another
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer: the three sets of witnesses came one right after the other, so the later ones knew what the earlier ones were doing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is when they came one after another, without a break.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second way to answer רב כהנא's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of needing hand signals, רב אשי says it is enough that the witnesses came in a row. When the testimonies follow each other directly, each set obviously sees what is being built, so they cannot say they did not know.

keyTerms.meaning: In a row, one right after another

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
When they came one after another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same challenge from step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Witnesses on the same day might not know about each other
steps.terutzMaskana: Coming one right after the other shows they knew

steps.title: רבינא: they knew the owner but not the ox
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the witnesses knew who the owner was but could not identify the ox. So they could not have come only for חצי נזק. Their only purpose must have been to make the ox a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It is a case where they recognize the owner of the ox but do not recognize the ox.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a third answer to רב כהנא's challenge. This one is based on what the witnesses could and could not identify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חצי נזק for a תם is paid only from the ox itself, so witnesses who cannot identify the ox cannot make anyone pay that way. Their testimony only matters for making the ox a מועד, which brings נזק שלם paid from the owner's own property. So the excuse 'we only came for half damage' does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Recognize, know
The owner of the ox

steps.whatToRemember: The proof that ייעוד is on the ox depends on the witnesses knowing about each other. The גמרא gives three ways this could be true: they signaled to each other, they came in a row (רב אשי), or they knew only the owner and not the ox (רבינא).
steps.whyThisMatters: רבינא's answer depends on the basic difference between a תם, which pays half only from the ox's own body, and a מועד, which pays in full from the owner's property.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Where they recognize the owner of the ox,
but do not recognize the ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the challenge from step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The last witnesses could say they came only for חצי נזק
steps.terutzMaskana: They could not identify the ox, so חצי נזק was impossible and their only purpose was to make it a מועד

steps.title: How can they warn about an ox they can't identify?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבינא's answer. If the witnesses don't know which ox it is, how can they give a warning that makes it a מועד?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do they give the warning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבינא from Step 5. A warning (ייעוד) seems to need a specific ox, and these witnesses could not point to one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To make an ox a מועד, the owner has to be warned. רבינא said the witnesses knew the owner but not the ox. So the גמרא asks what such a warning could even look like.

keyTerms.meaning: How?
They give the formal warning (ייעוד) that makes an ox a מועד

phrases.english: But how do they warn him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the workability of רבינא's answer in Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's case of witnesses who know the owner but not the ox
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A warning seems to need an identified ox, and here no ox can be identified.

steps.title: The warning: guard your whole herd
steps.stepSummary: The witnesses tell the owner that he has a goring ox somewhere in his herd, so he must guard all of his cattle.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say to him: You have a goring ox among your cattle, so you need to guard all your cattle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the warning is given to the owner in a general way. He is told that some ox in his herd gores.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warning does not have to name one ox. It is enough that the owner hears there is a goring ox in his herd. Now he has to guard every animal, which is exactly what a warning is meant to achieve.

keyTerms.meaning: A goring ox
Cattle, the herd
To guard

steps.whatToRemember: A ייעוד can be given to the owner without identifying the specific ox. He is told to guard his whole herd.

phrases.english: They say:
You have a goring ox among your cattle,
you need to guard all the cattle.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמְרִי תּוֹרָא נַגְּחָנָא אִית לָךְ בְּבַקְרָךְ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what the warning consists of
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A warning must point to a specific ox.
steps.terutzMaskana: A general warning to the owner about his herd is enough.

steps.title: Is the owner liable if someone else sets his dog on a person?
steps.stepSummary: A new question is raised. If one person sets another person's dog on a third person, the one who did it is surely פטור. Is the dog's owner liable?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: If someone sets his friend's dog on another person, what is the law? The one who set the dog on him is surely פטור. What about the dog's owner? Can the owner say, 'What did I do to him?' Or do we tell the owner, 'You knew your dog attacks when people set it on someone, so you should not have kept it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand-new topic with a question (איבעיא). It asks whether a dog's owner pays when someone else sets the dog on a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one who set the dog on the person is פטור because he did not do the damage himself, and it is not his property. The question is only about the owner. One side says the owner did nothing wrong. The other side says he knew his dog reacts this way, so keeping it makes him responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the חכמים
Sets an animal on someone, sics it on him
The owner of the dog
To keep it

steps.whyThisMatters: This question sets up the next steps. Two proofs will be brought, and both will be rejected.

phrases.english: They asked:

phrases.aramaic: הַמְשַׁסֶּה כַּלְבּוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ בַּחֲבֵירוֹ, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: One who sets his friend's dog on another person, what is the law?
The one who set it on him is surely exempt;
the dog's owner, what?
Do we say he can say to him:
Me, what did I do to him?
phrases.notes: The owner is speaking to the injured person.

phrases.english: Or perhaps we say to him:
Since you know about your dog
that when people set it on someone, it gets stirred up and attacks,
shouldn't you not have kept it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִבַּעְיָא לְהוּ הַמְשַׁסֶּה כַּלְבּוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ בַּחֲבֵירוֹ מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, not connected to the ייעוד discussion
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the dog's owner liable when a third party sets the dog on someone?

steps.title: רבי זירא's proof from children petting an ox
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא brings a ברייתא. An ox becomes תם again if children pet it and it does not gore. This implies that if it does gore, the owner is liable, even though the children stirred it up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Come and hear. An ox is תם again when children pet it and it does not gore. This implies that if it gores, the owner is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא tries to answer the question of Step 8. He reads an inference from a ברייתא about an ox becoming תם again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Children poking at an ox is like someone stirring up an animal. רבי זירא reads the ברייתא to mean that if the ox gores in that situation, the owner pays. If that is right, the dog's owner would also be liable when someone sets his dog on a person.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, which introduces a proof
An ox that is not a known gorer
Touching, petting, poking

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: Come and hear:
And it is תם again when the children pet it,
and it does not gore.
This implies: if it gores, he is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of Step 8
steps.raayaObject: The dog's owner is liable when someone else sets the dog on a person
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: an ox is תם again when children pet it and it does not gore

steps.title: אביי: the ברייתא only says it stays a מועד
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. The ברייתא never says the owner is liable. It may only mean that if the ox gores, it does not become תם again, and the owner does not pay for that goring.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Does it say 'if it gored he is liable'? Maybe it means that if it gored, it is not תם, but for that goring he is not liable.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down רבי זירא's proof by reading the ברייתא another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is only about status, meaning whether the ox goes back to being תם. If it gores while children poke it, it just stays a מועד. That says nothing about paying for that goring, so nothing can be proven about liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it actually say?
It is not תם, it stays a מועד
A goring

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the owner is פטור for sure. He is only showing that the ברייתא does not prove he is liable.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, מִי קָתָנֵי: נָגַח חַיָּיב?
phrases.english: אביי said: Does it teach 'if it gored, he is liable'?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא הָא נָגַח – לָא הָוֵי תָּם;
phrases.english: Maybe it means: if it gored, it is not תם;
and for that goring he is not liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי מִי קָתָנֵי נָגַח חַיָּיב
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The question itself stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is about the ox's status, not about paying for damage.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה about setting a dog on someone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה. One who sets a dog or a snake on someone is פטור. It suggests this means only the one who set the animal is פטור, while the dog's owner is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If he set a dog on him, or set a snake on him, he is פטור. Doesn't this mean the one who set it is פטור, but the dog's owner is liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second proof for the question of Step 8, this time from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'פטור' only about the one who set the animal on the person. The גמרא reads its silence about the owner as a hint that the owner is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: He set an animal on someone
A snake
Isn't it that... (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he set the dog on him,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in סנהדרין about someone who causes another person's death through an animal.

phrases.english: or set a snake on him, he is exempt.
What, isn't it that the one who set it is exempt,
but the dog's owner is liable?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע שִׁיסָּה בּוֹ אֶת הַכֶּלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second attempt to answer the question of Step 8, after Step 10 rejected the first
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: one who set a dog or snake on someone is פטור

steps.title: Rejected: even the one who set it is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Read the משנה as saying that even the one who set the dog is פטור, and the owner is too.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Say: even the one who set it is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof, so the question from Step 8 is still unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אף' (even) changes the reading. The משנה may mean that not only the owner but even the one who set the dog is פטור. So it cannot prove the owner is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, meaning read it this way
Even, also

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs (the ברייתא and the משנה) were rejected. We still do not know whether the dog's owner is liable when someone else sets his dog on a person.

phrases.english: No; say: even the one who set it is exempt.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only this proof is rejected. The question stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be read to exempt both the owner and the one who set the dog.

steps.title: רבא: if the victim set the dog on himself, the owner is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that even if the owner is liable when the dog is set on someone else, he is פטור when the victim himself set the dog on himself. The reason is the rule כל המשנה ובא אחר ושינה בו פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even if you say that when someone sets another person's dog on a third person, the owner is liable, if the person set the dog on himself, the owner is exempt. What is the reason? Anyone who acts abnormally, and then someone else comes and acts abnormally against him, the other one is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling for the case where the victim is the one who stirred up the dog against himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question from Step 8 is still open, so רבא says 'even if you say' the owner is liable. Even on that view, the owner is פטור when the victim stirred up the dog himself. The victim acted abnormally first, so he cannot claim for the dog's abnormal biting.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say: granting one side of an open question
One who sets or incites an animal against someone
He set it on himself
Anyone who acts out of the normal way
What is the reason?

steps.confusionAlert: 'He set it on himself' means the victim stirred up the dog and then got bitten. It does not mean the owner set his own dog.

phrases.english: Rava said: Even if you say:

phrases.aramaic: הַמְשַׁסֶּה כַּלְבּוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ בַּחֲבֵירוֹ – חַיָּיב;
phrases.english: one who sets another's dog on another person: liable;
phrases.notes: Following the question from Step 8, 'liable' here means the dog's owner has to pay.

phrases.english: if he set it on himself, exempt.
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמְשַׁנֶּה, וּבָא אַחֵר וְשִׁינָּה בּוֹ – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: Anyone who acts abnormally, and another came and acted abnormally against him, is exempt.
phrases.notes: The one who is exempt is the second one, here the dog's owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The question from Steps 8-12 was left open. רבא adds a side ruling that holds on either answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the victim incited the dog against himself, the owner is פטור, because whoever acts abnormally first cannot claim for another's abnormal act against him.

steps.title: רב פפא brings support from ריש לקיש's two cows
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא tells רבא that ריש לקיש said something matching his rule. If a walking cow kicks a cow lying in the street, the walking cow's owner is פטור. If the lying cow kicks the walking one, its owner is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: It was said in the name of ריש לקיש like you. ריש לקיש said: There are two cows in the public domain, one lying down and one walking. If the walking one kicked the lying one, it is exempt. If the lying one kicked the walking one, it is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a ruling of ריש לקיש that seems to fit רבא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lying down in the street is not normal, so the lying cow acted abnormally first. When the walking cow then kicks it, the walking cow's owner is פטור. That looks exactly like רבא's rule that the one who acted abnormally first cannot complain.

keyTerms.meaning: Like you, in agreement with your view
The public domain, such as a street
Lying down
Walking
Kicked

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
It was stated in the name of Reish Lakish like you,
as Reish Lakish said:
Two cows in the public domain,
one lying down and one walking,
and the walking one kicked the lying one: exempt.
The lying one kicked the walking one: liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבא's rule from Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that whoever acts abnormally first cannot claim for another's abnormal act against him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's ruling about a walking cow that kicks a cow lying in the public domain.

steps.title: רבא: in that case I would make the owner pay
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the support. In the cow case he would hold the walking cow's owner liable, because the lying cow can say: you may walk over me, but you may not kick me.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: In that case, I would hold him liable. We say to the walking cow: You have the right to walk over me, but you have no right to kick me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא says ריש לקיש's case is not the same as his rule, and he would actually rule the opposite there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lying in the street only gives the walking cow permission to step over or on the lying cow. Kicking goes beyond that permission, so the walking cow's owner pays. In רבא's dog case, the victim himself caused the very attack he suffered, which is why the owner is פטור there.

keyTerms.meaning: I would certainly hold him liable
Permission, a right
To walk over me
To kick me

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: the victim who stirs up a dog against himself cannot collect from the owner. But in the case of the cow lying in the street, רבא would make the walking cow's owner pay for a kick, since lying in the way only allows walking over it, not kicking.

phrases.english: He said to him: I,
in that case, would certainly hold him liable,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the owner of the walking cow that kicked.

phrases.english: because we say to it:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אִית לָךְ רְשׁוּתָא – לְסַגּוֹיֵי עֲלַי;
phrases.english: You do have permission to walk over me;
phrases.notes: The lying cow is the one 'speaking' here, to the walking cow.

phrases.english: to kick me, you have no permission.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא – בְּהָהִיא חַיּוֹבֵי מְחַיֵּיבְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support רב פפא brought in Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the idea that ריש לקיש's ruling matches רבא's rule. רבא's own ruling still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The lying cow's abnormal act only allows walking over it, not kicking it, so the cases are not the same.

steps.title: New משנה: an ox damaging in the victim's property
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains the earlier mention of 'an ox that damages in the victim's property.' In the public domain, goring, pushing, biting, lying on, or kicking pays חצי נזק. In the victim's property, רבי טרפון says נזק שלם and the חכמים say חצי נזק.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An ox that damages in the property of the injured party, how so? If it gored, pushed, bit, lay down on, or kicked: in the public domain, the owner pays half the damage. In the property of the injured party, רבי טרפון says full damage, and the חכמים say half damage.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains the case of an ox damaging in the victim's property, which was mentioned in an earlier משנה, and records a מחלוקת about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These five actions are not the normal way for an ox to behave, so in the public domain an ox that is not known for this (תם) pays only חצי נזק. The question is whether damage done in the victim's own property raises the payment. רבי טרפון says yes, to נזק שלם, while the חכמים say it stays at חצי נזק.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (short for מתניתין)
The property of the injured party
Pushed with its body
Lay down on something
Half the cost of the damage
Full cost of the damage

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה opens a new discussion about whether the place where damage happens changes how much the owner pays.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
An ox that damages in the property of the injured party: how so?
phrases.notes: This picks up a phrase from an earlier משנה (15b) that listed animals considered מועד.

phrases.english: It gored, pushed, bit, lay down on, or kicked;
in the public domain, he pays half the damage.

phrases.aramaic: בִּרְשׁוּת הַנִּיזָּק – רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: נֶזֶק שָׁלֵם,
phrases.english: In the property of the injured party, Rabbi Tarfon says: full damage,
and the Rabbis say: half damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שׁוֹר הַמַּזִּיק בִּרְשׁוּת הַנִּיזָּק, כֵּיצַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not connected to the dog and cow discussion before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the public domain, an ox that gores, pushes, bites, lies on, or kicks pays חצי נזק. In the victim's property, רבי טרפון says נזק שלם and the חכמים say חצי נזק.

steps.title: רבי טרפון's logical argument for full payment
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון brings a קל וחומר. If the Torah is strict with שן and רגל in רשות הניזק, even though they are exempt in רשות הרבים, then it should surely be strict with קרן in רשות הניזק, since קרן already pays in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון said to them: שן and רגל get off completely in the public domain, yet in the victim's property they pay full damage. קרן already pays half damage in the public domain. So shouldn't קרן pay full damage in the victim's property?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון proves his ruling from Step 16, that קרן in רשות הניזק pays נזק שלם. He does it with a קל וחומר, which is an 'all the more so' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where the Torah is lenient (רשות הרבים), שן and רגל pay nothing, but קרן still pays half. So קרן is the more serious case. When we move to רשות הניזק, שן and רגל jump up to full payment, so קרן, the stricter one, should jump up to full payment too.

keyTerms.meaning: Tooth: damage done when an animal eats something
Foot: damage done when an animal tramples something as it walks
Horn: damage done on purpose, like goring
was lenient / was strict
is it not logical? This is the classic wording of a קל וחומר

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon said to them:
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the חכמים, who said in Step 16 that the owner pays only half.

phrases.english: If in a place where [the Torah] was lenient
with Tooth and with Foot
in the public domain, where he is exempt;
it was strict with them in the victim's property,
to pay full damage;
then a place where it was strict with Horn,
in the public domain, to pay half damage;
is it not logical that we should be strict with it
in the victim's property, to pay full damage?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לָהֶם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן: וּמָה בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁהֵקֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי טרפון's ruling of נזק שלם in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רבי טרפון's ruling that קרן in רשות הניזק pays נזק שלם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from שן and רגל, which go from exempt in רשות הרבים to נזק שלם in רשות הניזק.

steps.title: The Sages answer: a derived law cannot exceed its source
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reply with the rule דיו לבא מן הדין להיות כנדון. A conclusion learned from a קל וחומר can only be as strict as the case it was learned from. So קרן in רשות הניזק pays חצי נזק, just as it does in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: It is enough for a law learned through logic to be equal to its source. Just as קרן pays half damage in the public domain, so too it pays half damage in the victim's property.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים block רבי טרפון's argument. They do not deny the logic, but they limit how far it can go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר does show that קרן in רשות הניזק should be at least as strict as קרן in רשות הרבים. But the rule of דיו says the result cannot go beyond the source. The source here is קרן in רשות הרבים, which pays half, so the result is also only half.

keyTerms.meaning: it is enough for it
the law that comes from logical reasoning, meaning the conclusion of a קל וחומר
the case being reasoned from, the source

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying רבי טרפון's קל וחומר is wrong. They agree it works. They only say its result is capped at the level of its source, so it gives חצי נזק and not נזק שלם.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule דיו לבא מן הדין להיות כנדון is a basic limit on every קל וחומר, and it shows up all over שס.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין –
phrases.english: They said to him: It is enough for what comes from logical reasoning
to be like the case it is learned from.
Just as in the public domain it is half damage,
so too in the victim's property it is half damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the full-payment result of רבי טרפון's קל וחומר in Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Partial. It accepts the קל וחומר but rejects its conclusion of נזק שלם.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The קל וחומר's result goes beyond its source, and that breaks the rule of דיו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קרן in רשות הניזק pays חצי נזק.

steps.title: רבי טרפון begins his counter-reply
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון starts to answer the חכמים with 'I too...'. The rest of his reply continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I too...
steps.whatsHappening: This is only a setup line. רבי טרפון is about to push back against the חכמים's rule of דיו, and his full argument comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'I too,' רבי טרפון signals that he will build a new argument. It will work even if we accept their limit, so the rule of דיו will not stop it. The content itself has not appeared yet.

keyTerms.meaning: I too / I also

phrases.english: He said to them: I too

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens רבי טרפון's response to the חכמים's דיו rejection in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's use of דיו to limit קרן in רשות הניזק to חצי נזק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי טרפון is starting a new argument meant to get around the דיו limit. Its details continue on the next amud.
